quote: opportunity for, you know, some kind of battery backup type approach.
stewart_read: Customer volunteers a battery-backup interest unprompted — a strong buying signal the rep correctly routes to a specialist rather than trying to explain Powerwall specs himself.
coaching_implication: Good instinct not to scope-creep into battery specs, but the rep never reflects the reason back later (e.g., in the confirmation) to reinforce why the appointment matters.

quote: It was Freedom at the time. I don't know if that's you guys now or
stewart_read: Customer discloses a prior installer and genuine confusion about company continuity, but the rep answers the identity question and pivots straight to ownership type without asking if the system works or its size.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep may have judged this out of scope for a setter call and left it for the specialist — but orphaned_flow explicitly calls for system-working status as a gate before booking.
coaching_implication: Ask 'is your system running fine currently?' before booking — a broken existing system changes what the specialist call should even cover.

quote: I think you seem to have a credit score above 670. Does that sound like the case for you?
stewart_read: Odd phrasing implies the rep is guessing/assuming the customer's credit rather than neutrally asking, which could bias a self-report either way.
coaching_implication: Ask the qualifier neutrally ('do you know if your credit is above 670?') rather than presupposing an answer.

quote: I'm not ready to have anybody come out yet. I kinda wanna understand cost, time frame, process, etcetera.
stewart_read: Customer sets an explicit condition on the appointment format (phone only, informational) before agreeing to book.
coaching_implication: This condition should travel into the handoff brief so the specialist doesn't push an in-person visit prematurely.

quote: I'll send you a text as well just with my number so you have, you know, point of contact
stewart_read: Rep offers his personal number as the point of contact, the exact anti-pattern flagged in the schema for privacy/scale exposure.
coaching_implication: Should route through the standard company text/follow-up channel, not a personal number.

quote: I'll get everything started then for you for Tuesday at four,
stewart_read: Day and time are locked, but the button_up is only partially run — no one-hour block statement, no explicit 'is that fair' handshake, and no no-driving/computer instruction.
coaching_implication: Add the missing button_up elements even on short calls — they predict show rate independent of call length.
